holdout_threshold — EMPROOF evaluate op

• Data kinds: signal × signal × signal × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.holdout_threshold(train_pos, train_neg, test_pos, test_neg, target_fpr: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import emproof; emproof.holdout_threshold(train_pos, train_neg, test_pos, test_neg, target_fpr: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsemproof.get("holdout_threshold"))

Usage

Chooses the threshold on the training side, and measures the evaluation on the other side (a higher score means "more suspicious").

tau = the smallest threshold at which the false-positive rate of the training negatives (components and pairs not planted) is at most target_fpr (the upper target_fpr quantile of the negative scores). Returned are tau and, for training and evaluation each, AUC, TPR, FPR and counts. Only the evaluation-side numbers are used for claims -- a TPR measured on the side where the threshold was chosen is always optimistic (the holdout discipline of evolve carved out as an op). AUC is Mann–Whitney (ties 0.5).

>>> r = holdout_threshold(tr_pos, tr_neg, te_pos, te_neg, target_fpr=0.05)

>>> r["tau"], r["test_auc"], r["test_tpr"], r["test_fpr"]
